newsitem.title: INDIA: India ICICI, SCICI merger on expected lines - analysts.
newsitem.headline: India ICICI, SCICI merger on expected lines - analysts.

text.p: Analysts said on Tuesday the merger of the Investment Credit and Investment Corporation of India Ltd (ICICI) and SCICI was on expected lines and unlikely to have any major impact on the industry.

"The swap ratio looks fair to both the companies," said Prabodh Agarwal, analyst at James Capel B&K. "We were expecting a ratio of one ICICI share for every 2.4 SCICI shares based on adjusted book value."

Earlier in the day, the boards of term lenders ICICI and SCICI approved a proposal to merge the two companies. The merger, effective from April 1, 1996, would involve an exchange of two ICICI shares of face value of ten rupees for every five shares of SCICI of face value ten rupees.
The merged entity would have a net worth of around 40 billion rupees and assets in excess of 330 billion rupees.
The merger seemed to favour ICICI more than SCICI, said another analyst who declined to be named.
"Maybe a ratio of 2.25 would have been more equitable than the current one," he said. "But then, in any merger, the larger player always gets better benefits."
Peregrine Capital India's analyst S.R Krishnan felt that in the current scenario, the merger seemed to be more beneficial to ICICI than SCICI.
"It looks beneficial to ICICI," Krishnan said. "ICICI is picking up a good quality asset portfolio."
However he felt that the swap ratio might have been calculated after discounting expectations of unimpressive future performance by SCICI.
"Besides SCICI is not bringing in any special expertise to ICICI that the latter lacks," he said.

Analysts said the merger would be beneficial to both companies as they were competing for similar funds' sources and clientele. They however did not feel that the merged entity would make any significant impact on the market.
"The merger is not going to create a giant," said Krishnan. "The Industrial Development Bank of India is still by far the largest player in the term lending market."
